weather_bureau_daily_f.source: Kitty Hawk Weather Bureau daily form, ECU digitization (digital.lib.ecu.edu/exhibits/wright/weather/19031217.html)
weather_bureau_daily_f.note: daily-summary form; NO hourly Bureau record exists

life_saving_station_log_f.source: Kitty Hawk Life Saving Station log (same ECU page)

ice_on_puddles.note: the famous ice line is from Orville's 1913 'How We Made the First Flight', NOT the day-of diary (which records only wind)

station_inhg.source: Life Saving Station log: 30.1 inHg at midnight/sunrise/noon/sunset
station_inhg.note: one instrument, 0.1-inHg resolution; near-sea-level station pressure ~101.9 kPa

wind.diary_verbatim: The wind, according to our anemometers at this time, was blowing a little over 20 miles (corrected) 27 miles according to the Government anemometer

bureau_ledger.finding: the surviving Weather Bureau daily form records wind velocity as literally 'No Record' — the 27 mph government reading survives ONLY via Orville reporting observer Joseph J. Dosher's number; no government hourly wind sequence exists

gust_accounts: flight 3: 'a strong gust from the left'
after flight 4: a 'sudden gust' rolled and wrecked the machine (separate from the landing damage)

turbulence_intensity.note: no modern paper publishes a Dec-17 TI estimate; any value is a derivation

station_metadata.location: co-located with the Kitty Hawk Life Saving Station, Kitty Hawk village beach, ~4 mi N of the Kill Devil Hills camp; weather office 1875-1904; observer Joseph J. Dosher

anemometer.note: type and mounting height undocumented; Robinson cup was the era-standard Bureau instrument (inference, not record); the Wrights calibrated their Richard hand anemometers against this station

derived_air_state.doctrine: DERIVED values carry their derivation and are re-computed by the battery; they are never presented as measurements

rho_kg_m3.note: ~6% DENSER than standard sea level (1.225) — and the sim papers (Deters 2004-0211 effectively standard atmosphere; Culick/Jex coefficient-form) never used the cold-day density; Lawrence & Padfield credit 'low temperatures, high-density air, high winds' qualitatively

reynolds_flight.literature_note: the literature's '~1e6' (Lawrence & Padfield, single source) is an order-of-magnitude convention, not a computed Dec-17 value; L&P also quote ~10% CLmax loss at model Re 1e5

wind_reference_records.provenance: Orville diary, hand-held reading near the rail
Dosher's reading as reported in Orville's diary; the ledger itself records No Record; 1913 article extends to 24-27 over the flights

neutral_stability_declaration.basis: strong mechanically-mixed surface wind (>10 m/s), overcast winter morning over cold sea-adjacent sand — shear production dominates buoyancy
neutral_stability_declaration.caveat: stability class remains a DECLARED uncertainty axis (frame-conventions uncertainty-v1); the H-case ensemble may include weakly-stable members, labeled

z0_m_prior.basis: bare sand with sparse beach-grass tufts per 1903 photos; spans the Davenport-Wieringa sand band and the flyer-reference range; the site was grass-stabilized in the 1930s so MODERN roughness is not representative

displacement_height_m_prior.basis: sparse tufts, no canopy; essentially zero with allowance

dec17_ensemble_preregistration.doctrine: PRE-REGISTERED distribution parameters for the H-case ensemble. The historical control traces and gust time-series are UNKNOWN: any specific gust sequence is a REALIZATION drawn from these parameters bound to a PhysicalUncertaintyRealizationId — never a claimed reconstruction. This artifact must NEVER contain a gust trace (battery-gated).

parameters.name: wind_mean_mps_at_instrument
parameters.distribution: instrument mixture: wrights-hand-richard N(9.2, 0.5) | government-weather-bureau N(12.1, 0.7), reconciled through the log-law with the height priors

parameters.name: wind_direction_deg
parameters.distribution: N/NNE sector: uniform [0, 30] deg from true north

parameters.name: turbulence_intensity_sigma_u_over_U
parameters.basis: DERIVED (neutral surface layer over the z0 prior) — not a source value

dec17_ensemble_preregistration.gust_realization_rule: gust time-series are generated by fs-atmo (E3.3) from these parameters under the exact-discrete OU / Mann-class machinery; realization identity binds PhysicalRealizationAlgorithmId

huffman_1904_05.conditions: light/variable winds vs Kitty Hawk (qualitative, universal); catapult from 1904-09-07 to reach flying speed in near-calm

density_altitude_arithmetic.note: no source computes the summer-Dayton vs winter-KDH density/headwind trade explicitly; closest are L&P's qualitative sentence and AIAA 2001-0309's 1000-ft Dayton pressure-altitude convention (which applies to the Nov-21 Dayton prop tests, NOT Dec-17)

per_flight_logs.note: no published 1904-05 per-flight wind/temperature log; the Wrights' LoC diaries are the primary source to mine (future task)

no_claims: Records + derivations + pre-registered distributions. No reconstructed gust trace exists or may ever be added here; derived values are battery-recomputed; sim papers' standard-atmosphere assumption is a recorded correction opportunity, not an error claim.
